The data in the notice must match the labels on the containers: part number, quantity, delivery note number and container serial numbers.

5.2.4 The supplier must monitor its EDI connection every day and respond to a transmission failure within 1 hour. If the failure lasts more than 4 hours, the supplier and the Aurelia EDI team agree on a fallback by telephone and e-mail. Fallback documents are accepted only for a limited time and the supplier must clear the problem within 2 working days.

5.3 Forecasts and capacity

5.3.1 Forecasts are non-binding indications of expected demand. They cover 26 weeks and are refreshed every week. The first 4 weeks are described as the frozen horizon, and the following 4 weeks as the flexible horizon.

5.3.2 Suppliers must plan capacity to cover the forecast peak plus a flexibility reserve. The reserve is a minimum of 10 percent above the forecast for weeks 5 to 8 and a minimum of 20 percent above the forecast for weeks 1 to 4 compared with the quantities in the weekly delivery schedule issued 4 weeks earlier.

5.3.3 Each supplier must report its capacity status every quarter, and at once if it cannot meet the forecast quantities. The report states the weekly capacity per part number, the bottleneck, and the actions planned.

5.3.4 Before a model launch, the supplier takes part in a capacity run of 8 hours at the planned peak rate. The target for the run is a demonstrated rate of at least 105 percent of the peak daily quantity.

5.4 Delivery schedules and delivery windows

5.4.1 The delivery schedule is binding for the quantity and the date it states. The supplier must deliver exactly the called quantity, with no allowance for over-delivery or under-delivery unless Aurelia agrees in writing in advance. A delivery counts as on time only when the full quantity arrives inside the window.

5.4.2 A delivery window is the period in which the vehicle must arrive at the unloading point. Windows are set per plant and per unloading point. The standard windows are given below.

| Delivery type | Window length | Earliest arrival | Latest arrival |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard truck delivery, Modena | 60 minutes | 30 minutes before window start | At window end |
| Standard truck delivery, Cassino | 60 minutes | 30 minutes before window start | At window end |
| Standard truck delivery, Kragujevac | 120 minutes | 60 minutes before window start | At window end |
| Line-side delivery (daily multiple) | 30 minutes | 10 minutes before window start | At window end |
| Just-in-sequence delivery | 10 minutes | none | 10 minutes before required line time |

5.4.3 A vehicle that arrives before the earliest arrival time may be refused or made to wait. Waiting time is not charged to Aurelia. A vehicle that arrives after the window is unloaded as soon as capacity allows, and the delivery is recorded as late.

5.4.4 The supplier plans transit time with a safety margin appropriate to the route. For the road route from northern Italy to Modena, a minimum buffer of 3 hours is expected. For the route from Kragujevac suppliers to the plant, the buffer is a minimum of 6 hours, owing to border formalities.

5.4.5 Stock requirements: the supplier holds a finished goods safety stock sufficient for 3 working days for standard parts, and 5 working days for parts with long transport routes, unless the supply agreement says otherwise.

5.5 Delivery performance measurement

5.5.1 Aurelia measures delivery performance by supplier and plant every month. The main indicators are on-time delivery, quantity accuracy and the number of line interruptions caused by the supplier.

5.5.2 The targets and the escalation levels are as follows.

| Indicator | Target | Level 1 (written notice) | Level 2 (action plan) | Level 3 (management review) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| On-time delivery | 98.5 % or above | below 98.5 % | below 96.0 % | below 92.0 % |
| Quantity accuracy | 99.5 % or above | below 99.5 % | below 98.5 % | below 97.0 % |
| Line interruption minutes | 0 | any | above 20 min per month | above 60 min per month |
| ASN accuracy | 99.0 % or above | below 99.0 % | below 97.5 % | below 95.0 % |

5.5.3 At Level 2, the supplier presents an action plan within 5 working days. At Level 3, the supplier's plant manager attends a review at Aurelia and a monthly follow-up is held until the indicators have been back at target for 3 consecutive months.

5.5.4 The supplier receives its scorecard by working day 5 of the following month. The supplier may contest a data point within 10 working days, with evidence such as gate records or transport documents.

5.6 Premium freight

5.6.1 Premium freight means any transport at a higher cost or higher speed than the standard transport route, including special vehicles, courier shipments and air freight, used to recover a delivery.

5.6.2 Where premium freight is needed because of a cause within the supplier's control, the supplier bears all costs. These causes include late production, insufficient capacity, quality problems at the supplier, missing packaging, and late or wrong shipping data.

5.6.3 Where the cause is a change in Aurelia demand beyond the flexibility range in clause 5.3.2, Aurelia bears the cost, but only if the supplier has told the Aurelia planner as soon as it knew it could not meet the call.

5.6.4 Premium freight must be authorised in advance by the Aurelia logistics planner, who issues an authorisation number. Costs for which no number was issued will not be reimbursed, but will be charged to the supplier if the cause lies with the supplier.

5.6.5 Each supplier receives a monthly premium freight report. The target is zero events. A supplier with more than 3 premium freight events in a quarter, or with premium freight costs above EUR 5,000 in a quarter, must present a root cause analysis and a corrective action plan to Aurelia within 10 working days.

5.7 Line stoppages

5.7.1 If a supplier failure stops or is likely to stop an Aurelia line, the supplier must call the Aurelia plant logistics desk at once, at any hour, using the emergency number in the supplier contact sheet.

5.7.2 For each full minute of line stoppage caused by the supplier, Aurelia charges the line cost shown in the supply agreement. As a general guide, a stoppage at Modena final assembly is charged at EUR 410 per minute, at Cassino at EUR 285 per minute, and at Kragujevac at EUR 190 per minute. Aurelia may charge additional costs it can show, such as overtime and rescheduling.

5.7.3 After each stoppage, the supplier sends a short written explanation within 24 hours and a full analysis within 10 working days.

## 9. Nonconforming product and problem solving

6.1 Purpose and scope

This section defines how Aurelia and its suppliers handle nonconforming product, from the moment a problem is found to the moment its cause has been removed. It applies to production parts, service parts and tooling delivered to any Aurelia site, and to nonconformities found at Aurelia, at logistics partners, at dealers and in the field. The aim is to protect the customer, to contain the problem quickly and to prevent it from happening again.

6.2 Definitions

6.2.1 A nonconformity is any failure of a part, a process, a label or a delivery to meet the drawing, specification, order or this manual.

6.2.2 A complaint is Aurelia's formal notice to the supplier of a nonconformity. Complaints are sent electronically through the Aurelia supplier portal and by e-mail to the contact named in the supplier contact sheet.

6.2.3 Parts per million (ppm) is the number of nonconforming parts per million parts delivered, calculated by plant and by supplier on a rolling 12-month basis.

6.3 Complaint handling and response times

6.3.1 Aurelia assigns each complaint a severity class based on the effect of the problem. Class 1 means a safety-relevant or legally relevant effect, or a stoppage of a vehicle line. Class 2 means a defect that the customer would notice, or a part that cannot be assembled. Class 3 means a minor defect with no effect on function or assembly.

6.3.2 The supplier must meet the response times below. The time starts when the complaint is sent through the portal. Working days are counted by the Italian calendar, and for Class 1 the time is counted in clock hours, including weekends.

| Step | Class 1 | Class 2 | Class 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acknowledge complaint and name a contact | 2 hours | 1 working day | 2 working days |
| Containment at supplier, in transit and at Aurelia | 24 hours | 2 working days | 5 working days |
| Initial analysis and interim report (D1 to D3) | 48 hours | 3 working days | 5 working days |
| Root cause and corrective action plan (D4 to D6) | 10 working days | 15 working days | 20 working days |
| Final report (D7 to D8) | 30 working days | 40 working days | 60 working days |

6.3.3 Where a complete root cause analysis cannot be done within the time, the supplier must tell Aurelia in writing before the deadline, giving the reason and a new date. A later date is accepted only by Aurelia's quality engineer, and a maximum of one extension of 10 working days is allowed for each report.

6.3.4 The supplier must return suspect parts it holds, and parts returned by Aurelia for analysis, with a clear note of the complaint number. Aurelia provides return parts for analysis within 5 working days of a request, in quantities up to 10 parts.

6.4 Containment

6.4.1 The supplier must immediately check all stock at its premises, in transit, at logistics partners and at Aurelia, and must separate all suspect parts.

6.4.2 Containment measures must be effective for the full affected population. The supplier states the first good lot, shown by a lot number, serial number or date, and Aurelia uses this information to check its stock.

6.4.3 Until the cause is removed, the supplier must carry out additional inspection of 100 percent of each delivery, and must mark each container as inspected using the green sticker described in the packaging rules. Aurelia may ask for the inspection to be carried out by an external service at the supplier's expense, where the supplier's own containment is not sufficient. This is known as controlled shipping, and it lasts until the supplier proves 3 consecutive lots, or 4 weeks of delivery, without a recurrence.

6.4.4 Parts sorted or reworked at Aurelia, at a logistics partner or at a service provider on behalf of Aurelia are recorded by hours and quantity. These records are the basis for any charge.

6.5 Problem solving report format

6.5.1 Suppliers must report in the 8D format, using the Aurelia template available from the portal. Each report is written in English or Italian. Free-text sections must be specific. General statements such as "operator error" or "will pay more attention" are not acceptable causes or actions.

6.5.2 The content of each discipline is defined below.

| Discipline | Content required |
|---|---|
| D1 Team | Names, functions and contact details of at least three people, including a team leader with authority over the process |
| D2 Problem description | Is and is-not description: what, where, when, how many, with photographs and measured values |
| D3 Containment | Actions, stock quantities by location, responsible person, date and first good lot |
| D4 Root cause | Cause for occurrence and cause for escape, each with evidence from testing and a verified chain of why-questions |
| D5 Corrective actions | Chosen actions for both causes, with expected effect and planned date |
| D6 Implementation and verification | Evidence that the actions were put into place and measured effect, such as capability data and audit results |
| D7 Prevention | Transfer to similar parts, processes and plants; update of the risk analysis, control plan and work instructions |
| D8 Closing and recognition | Summary of the effect, lessons learned, and release of the team |

6.5.3 A report must show both why the defect was produced and why it was not detected before shipment. A report that deals with only one of these is returned to the supplier for revision and the response time continues to run.

6.5.4 Where a root cause analysis shows that the cause lies at a sub-supplier, the supplier remains Aurelia's single point of contact and is responsible for the sub-supplier's actions and for the cost.

6.5.5 Reports must be backed with data. Where a measuring system is part of the cause, the supplier provides evidence of the measuring system's repeatability and reproducibility, and the total variation attributed to the measuring system must be 10 percent or less of the tolerance.

6.6 Supplier performance indicators

6.6.1 Aurelia calculates the ppm value of each supplier every month. Parts found nonconforming at Aurelia, on the line or in the field count towards the figure, as long as the supplier is responsible.

6.6.2 Targets and escalation steps are as follows.

| Supplier ppm (rolling 12 months) | Rating | Required action |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 20 | Excellent | None |
| 21 to 50 | Good | Routine monitoring |
| 51 to 150 | Needs improvement | Improvement plan within 15 working days |
| 151 to 500 | Unsatisfactory | Quality review at the supplier and weekly status meetings |
| Above 500 | Critical | Management review at Aurelia and controlled shipping |

6.6.3 For each supplier, Aurelia also tracks the number of complaints, the rate of reports sent on time (target 95 percent or higher), and the number of repeat complaints, which are complaints with the same root cause within 24 months. Each repeat complaint is reviewed by Aurelia's supplier quality manager.

6.7 Chargebacks

6.7.1 The supplier bears the costs that arise from nonconforming product for which it is responsible. Aurelia charges only costs that it can show with records.

6.7.2 The following cost elements and rates apply, unless the supply agreement states other values.

| Cost element | Rate or basis |
|---|---|
| Administrative handling fee per complaint, Class 3 | EUR 150 |
| Administrative handling fee per complaint, Class 2 | EUR 350 |
| Administrative handling fee per complaint, Class 1 | EUR 900 |
| Sorting and rework at Aurelia | EUR 52 per labour hour |
| Production line stoppage | Line cost per minute as stated in the logistics rules |
| Part cost of scrapped material | Purchase price of the part, plus 12 percent handling |
| External laboratory analysis | Cost invoiced to Aurelia, without addition |
| Late 8D report | EUR 100 per working day, up to a maximum of EUR 1,500 per report |

6.7.3 Aurelia sends the supplier a debit note with supporting records, such as hours, quantities and invoices. The supplier has 20 working days to object with evidence. A debit note without objection is settled with the next payment.

6.7.4 Costs arising from vehicle recalls, field actions and warranty claims are dealt with under the quality and warranty provisions of the supply agreement, and are not covered in this manual.

6.7.5 Where a supplier considers that a complaint is not justified, it must still meet the containment and acknowledgement times. A disagreement does not stop the clock. The supplier states its reasons with measurement data, and Aurelia's quality engineer reviews them within 5 working days.

6.8 Escalation and cooperation

6.8.1 If a supplier repeatedly fails to meet the response times in this section, Aurelia may ask for a review of the supplier's problem solving process on site. The review is carried out by the Aurelia supplier quality engineer and takes about one day.

6.8.2 Suppliers are asked to keep a standing team for problem solving, to train their employees in the 8D method, and to name a deputy for each contact, so that complaints sent outside normal hours, or during holidays, are dealt with without delay.

6.8.3 Aurelia and the supplier hold a joint quality meeting at least twice a year to review the ppm trend, repeat complaints and open actions, and to agree the priorities for the following six months.

## 10. Warranty and field returns

4.1 Purpose and scope

This section sets out how Aurelia Automobili S.p.A. ("Aurelia") handles parts returned from the field, how no-trouble-found (NTF) results are analysed, how warranty costs are recovered from suppliers, and how return parts are stored and released. It applies to every supplier of series-production parts, service parts and accessories fitted to vehicles sold under the Aurelia brand, including parts supplied through a sub-tier source. The aim is to find the true cause of each field failure quickly, to charge cost to the party that caused it, and to keep the evidence needed to prove it.

4.2 Warranty periods and coverage

Unless the supply agreement states otherwise, the supplier's liability follows the vehicle warranty that Aurelia gives to the end customer, plus a supplier tail. The standard periods are shown below.

| Part category | Vehicle warranty | Supplier liability period | Mileage limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Body, trim and chassis hardware | 36 months | 48 months | 80,000 km |
| Powertrain mechanical | 48 months | 60 months | 100,000 km |
| Electrical and electronic modules | 36 months | 54 months | 90,000 km |
| Battery and high-voltage components | 96 months | 108 months | 160,000 km |
| Service and accessory parts | 24 months | 30 months | not applicable |

The period starts on the vehicle's in-service date as recorded in the Aurelia dealer system. For service parts it starts on the date of fitting. A part replaced under warranty carries the remaining period of the original warranty or 12 months, whichever is longer.

4.3 Return flow

A dealer who replaces a part under warranty tags it with the claim number, vehicle identification number, mileage and fault description. Tagged parts are sent to one of three Aurelia return centres: Modena, Brno or Leipzig. The return centre carries out the following steps.

1. Goods receipt and scan of the part label within 2 working days of arrival.
2. Visual check and photograph of the part as received, before any cleaning.
3. Assignment to a supplier and a part family, using the part number and date code.
4. Release to the supplier or to the Aurelia analysis laboratory, depending on the part class.

The supplier receives a return notice through the supplier portal within 5 working days of goods receipt. Parts must not be cleaned, bench-tested or opened by anyone before the analysis plan has been agreed, because this destroys evidence of the failure condition.

4.4 Analysis and response times

The supplier must analyse each returned part and give a written finding. Targets are set by the part class and are counted in calendar days from the date the part is made available to the supplier.

| Return class | Description | Initial finding | Full analysis with cause | Corrective action plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Safety-relevant or vehicle immobilised | 3 days | 10 days | 15 days |
| B | Function lost, vehicle drivable | 7 days | 20 days | 30 days |
| C | Comfort, noise or appearance | 10 days | 30 days | 45 days |

The finding must state the failure mode, the failure location on the part, the process step or design feature that caused it, and the evidence used. Statements such as "cause unknown" or "customer misuse" are accepted only when backed by measured data and photographs. A supplier that needs more time must ask in writing before the target date and give a reason. Aurelia may grant up to 10 extra days.

4.5 No-trouble-found analysis

A part is recorded as NTF when the supplier's first bench test does not reproduce the fault the dealer described. NTF is not a final result. It is a trigger for a deeper analysis, because intermittent faults often hide behind a normal bench result. The following steps apply to every NTF part.

1. Repeat the test under the conditions recorded in the claim: temperature, supply voltage, vibration and humidity where known.
2. Read stored fault memory and operating-hour counters from the part, where it has them.
3. Run a thermal cycling test of at least 50 cycles between -40 °C and +105 °C, or the cycle defined in the part specification if it is more demanding.
4. Inspect connectors, seals and solder joints under at least 20x magnification, and perform a cross-section where an indication is seen.
5. Compare the part with 5 retained samples from the same production week.

If these steps still give no fault, the supplier submits an NTF record with the test data attached. Aurelia reviews the record together with vehicle data, including the diagnostic trouble codes and the repair history of the vehicle. Where the vehicle data points to a software, wiring or diagnostic-logic issue in the vehicle, the cost stays with Aurelia. Where it points to the part, the supplier carries the cost even though the bench test was normal.

Aurelia tracks NTF as a rate for each part family. The NTF rate is the number of returned parts with no fault found divided by all returned parts of that family in a rolling 6-month period. The reference value is 30 percent for electronic modules and 15 percent for mechanical parts. A supplier whose NTF rate exceeds the reference value for 2 consecutive months must submit a test-capability review, covering test coverage, equipment accuracy and the operator method. A repeat-fit rule also applies: if the same part number is returned from the same vehicle twice with an NTF result, the third return is analysed jointly at the Aurelia laboratory.

4.6 Cost recovery

When the analysis or the vehicle data shows that the part caused the failure, Aurelia recovers cost from the supplier. The recoverable items are listed below.

| Cost element | Basis of charge | Example rate |
|---|---|---|
| Replacement part | Purchase price at the time of supply | Price list value |
| Dealer labour | Official repair time multiplied by the dealer labour rate | EUR 78 per hour |
| Diagnosis time | Actual time up to a cap | Up to 1.5 hours per claim |
| Transport and towing | Invoice value | At cost |
| Return handling and analysis | Fixed fee per part | EUR 42 per part |
| Goodwill and courtesy vehicle | Share of invoice value when the part is the cause | 100 percent |

For an individual claim, Aurelia sends a debit note once the cause has been assigned. For a batch problem, where a defect affects a population of vehicles, the supplier carries the full cost of the containment and service action. Aurelia and the supplier agree a recovery estimate, which is then adjusted against actual claims every quarter. A supplier may dispute a charge within 30 days of the debit note. The dispute must include data showing that the part was not the cause. Charges not disputed within 30 days are settled by deduction from the next payment run.

A flat rate applies to low-value claims. Where the total cost of a claim is below EUR 60, Aurelia and the supplier may agree a monthly lump sum based on the claim rate of the previous 12 months, so that individual analysis is not needed for each part.

4.7 Return parts: storage, release and disposal

Return centres keep every returned part, in its tagged bag and in a controlled rack, for at least 12 months after goods receipt. Parts with safety relevance (class A) are held for 36 months. Parts released to a supplier must be returned to Aurelia within 30 days unless Aurelia states in writing that the supplier may keep them. A part used for destructive testing must be photographed in each step, and the remains must be returned or disposed of as instructed. The chain of custody, from dealer to return centre to supplier and back, is recorded in the portal with date, name and condition. A part with a broken chain of custody cannot support a dispute by either party. Parts are scrapped only after the retention period has ended and after the supplier has confirmed there is no further analysis planned.

## 11. Supplier performance scorecard and escalation

5.1 Purpose

Aurelia measures every active supplier on the same set of indicators so that quality, delivery and responsiveness can be compared fairly and acted on early. This section describes the scorecard, the key performance indicators (KPIs), the levels of escalation, and the new business hold. The scorecard is calculated monthly and published on the supplier portal by the 8th working day of the following month. Suppliers are expected to review it each month and to react to any indicator that is outside the target.

5.2 Scorecard structure

The overall score is a number from 0 to 100. It combines five groups of indicators. The weights below apply to production suppliers. For service-parts suppliers the delivery group carries 30 points and the cost group carries 5 points.

| Group | Weight (points) | Main indicators |
|---|---|---|
| Delivered quality | 35 | Parts per million (PPM) defective, number of line stoppages |
| Field quality | 25 | Claims per 1,000 vehicles, warranty cost per vehicle |
| Delivery | 20 | On-time delivery rate, premium freight events |
| Responsiveness | 12 | Timeliness of corrective action, quality of analysis |
| Cost and commercial | 8 | Price-reduction delivery, invoice accuracy |

A supplier receives a rating based on the total score: A for 90 to 100 points, B for 75 to 89, C for 60 to 74, and D for below 60.

5.3 Key performance indicators and targets

The table below gives the standard targets. Individual agreements may set tighter values for critical parts.

| KPI | Definition | Target | Limit for escalation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incoming PPM | Defective parts found at Aurelia plants per million delivered, rolling 3 months | 20 or below | Above 100 |
| Line stoppage | Minutes of assembly line stopped because of the supplier part | 0 | More than 15 minutes in a month |
| Field claim rate | Claims per 1,000 vehicles in the first 12 months in service | 1.5 or below | Above 4.0 |
| On-time delivery | Deliveries within the agreed window of plus or minus 1 day | 98.5 percent or above | Below 95.0 percent |
| Premium freight | Number of expedited shipments caused by the supplier | 0 | 2 or more in a quarter |
| Corrective action timeliness | Percentage of required responses delivered by the due date | 95 percent or above | Below 80 percent |
| Analysis quality | Score from 1 to 5 given by Aurelia engineers to each analysis | 4.0 or above | Below 3.0 |

PPM is calculated on the number of parts delivered, not the number of deliveries. A defect found at an Aurelia plant and traced to a sub-tier source counts against the direct supplier. Defects that are the result of an Aurelia drawing error or incorrect handling at the plant are removed from the calculation after review by the Aurelia supplier quality engineer.

5.4 Levels of escalation

Escalation has four levels. A supplier enters a level when a trigger is met and leaves it when the exit conditions have been met. The levels are intended to increase management attention in proportion to the risk to Aurelia production and customers.

| Level | Name | Typical trigger | Required supplier action | Aurelia action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Standard | Score 75 or above, no KPI over the limit | Normal monthly review | Annual review meeting |
| 1 | Watch | Score 60 to 74, or any one KPI over the limit for 2 months | Written improvement plan within 10 working days | Monthly call with the supplier quality manager |
| 2 | Formal action | Score below 60 for 2 months, or a repeat issue with the same cause | Plan led by the supplier's plant manager; weekly status to Aurelia | On-site review within 20 working days; increased inspection at the supplier plant or the Aurelia plant |
| 3 | Executive | No measurable improvement after 90 days at level 2, or a serious customer-relevant failure | Plan led by the supplier's chief executive; resident quality support | Meeting with the Aurelia purchasing director; costs of extra inspection charged to the supplier |

A single event can move a supplier directly to level 2 or 3 where it has caused a vehicle stop-sale, a safety-relevant field action, or more than 24 hours of lost vehicle production.

5.5 Additional inspection

From level 2 onward, Aurelia may require one of two controlled-shipping stages. In the first stage the supplier adds its own extra inspection at its plant and sends the inspection records with each delivery. In the second stage a third-party inspector is placed at the supplier plant or at an Aurelia sorting site. The supplier pays the cost of this inspector, at the rate of EUR 46 per hour as of the date of this manual, plus any travel cost. Controlled shipping continues until the supplier has delivered 3 consecutive months with no defect found by the extra inspection and a PPM value below the limit.

5.6 New business hold

A new business hold stops Aurelia from awarding new parts, new vehicle programmes or additional volume to the supplier. It does not stop deliveries or service of existing parts. The hold rules are as follows.

1. A supplier at level 2 is placed on a conditional hold. New quotations are accepted, but no award is made without the written decision of the purchasing director and the head of quality.
2. A supplier at level 3 is placed on a full hold. No quotation request is sent, and the supplier is removed from the sourcing lists for new programmes.
3. A supplier with a rating of D in 2 consecutive quarters is placed on a conditional hold, even if no escalation trigger has been met.
4. The hold applies to all Aurelia plants and to all product lines of the supplier legal entity. Where a quality issue is confined to one site of the supplier, the hold applies to that site only.

The supplier is told of the hold by letter from the head of purchasing and is given the reason, the data and the exit conditions.

5.7 Exit from escalation and hold

To leave level 3 and move to level 2, the supplier must show 3 consecutive months with all KPIs inside the limits. To leave level 2 and move to level 1, 3 months with all KPIs inside the limits and a successful on-site review are required. Leaving level 1 requires 3 months with a score of 75 or above. A new business hold is lifted when the supplier has returned to level 1 or lower and has held that level for at least 6 months. Aurelia keeps a record of every change of level and the reasons for it. A supplier may ask for a review of its score within 15 working days of publication by sending evidence of a data error to the supplier quality engineer; the corrected score is published in the following month.

## 12. Traceability, records retention and audits

6.1 Purpose and principle

If a defect is found in the field, Aurelia must be able to say within hours which vehicles contain the affected parts, and the supplier must be able to say which material, machine, people and process conditions were behind them. This section sets the minimum rules for lot traceability, the retention periods for quality records, and the schedule of audits that Aurelia carries out at supplier sites. The rules apply to the supplier and are to be passed on to its sub-tier sources for any element that appears in the traceability chain.

6.2 Lot traceability requirements

Every part must carry a mark that links it to a production lot. The mark is applied to the part, or where this is not possible to the smallest package, and must stay legible for the life of the part. The mark shows at least the supplier code, the Aurelia part number, the date of manufacture and a lot or serial number. Parts of safety relevance and electronic modules must be marked with a unique serial number in a machine-readable 2D code.

A lot is the quantity produced from one batch of raw material, on one machine or line, in one setup and in no more than one shift. Lot size must not exceed the limits below unless Aurelia agrees a different figure.

| Part type | Maximum lot size | Marking | Traceability depth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Safety-relevant parts | 1 part (serial) | 2D code on part | Raw material, process data, test result, operator |
| Electronic modules | 1 part (serial) | 2D code on part | Component lots, board lot, test result |
| Machined and cast parts | 1,000 parts or 1 shift | Date code and lot on part | Raw material heat or batch, machine, tool change |
| Plastic and trim parts | 2,500 parts or 1 shift | Date code on part or box | Granulate batch, tool, machine |
| Fasteners and standard parts | 10,000 parts | Label on box | Supplier lot, delivery note |

Traceability must work in two directions. Forward tracing identifies every delivery that contains a given raw material lot or component lot. Backward tracing identifies, from a part number and date code, the lots of material and components used. The supplier must prove this ability on request. The required response time for a trace query is 4 hours for the first answer and 24 hours for a full list of affected parts and the stock location of each. A supplier must also run its own trace test twice a year using a randomly selected finished part, and the exercise must reach all the way to raw material in no more than 8 hours.

6.3 Data linked to each lot

For each lot the supplier keeps a record that contains the following items.

1. Identification of the raw material or component lots, with the certificate of the material source.
2. The machine or line, the tool or fixture number, and the date and time of setup.
3. Process parameters that are specified as critical on the control plan, with values or a statement that the values were inside limits.
4. Results of in-process checks and final tests, including measured values for characteristics marked as special.
5. Identification of the rework or sorting performed, with quantity and date.
6. Quantities produced, scrapped, shipped, and the delivery notes used.

Paper or electronic records are both accepted. Electronic records must be backed up at least daily, stored at a second location, and readable throughout the retention period even when software or equipment is replaced.

6.4 Records retention periods

The retention period is counted from the end of series supply of the part to Aurelia, unless a different start is shown in the table. If a record has a retention period of the end of supply plus a number of years, the supplier must keep the record until that date.

| Record type | Retention period |
|---|---|
| Lot traceability records for safety-relevant parts | End of supply plus 20 years |
| Lot traceability records for other parts | End of supply plus 15 years |
| Control plans, process flow diagrams and failure analysis of the process | End of supply plus 15 years |
| Final inspection and test results | 15 years from date of production |
| Measurement system and gauge calibration records | 10 years from date of calibration |
| Corrective action records and field return analyses | End of supply plus 15 years |
| Internal and external audit records | 10 years from date of the audit |
| Training and qualification records of operators on special processes | 10 years from end of employment or qualification |
| Delivery notes and packing lists | 10 years from date of delivery |
| Retained samples (see 6.5) | 3 years from date of production, or 5 years for safety-relevant parts |

If Aurelia opens a quality investigation or a legal matter, it may ask the supplier to keep certain records for longer. Such a request is made in writing, and the supplier must keep the named records until Aurelia releases them in writing. At the end of the retention period the supplier destroys the records in a way that prevents their reuse, and keeps a short log of what was destroyed and when.

6.5 Retained samples

For every production lot of safety-relevant parts the supplier keeps 5 retained samples. For other parts the supplier keeps 3 samples per week of production. The samples are stored in a labelled and controlled area at room conditions, and they are used for comparison with parts returned from the field. Retained samples must be made available to Aurelia within 5 working days of a request.

6.6 Audit schedule

Aurelia audits supplier sites on a schedule that depends on risk. The risk class is set by the supplier quality manager once a year using the scorecard rating, the criticality of the supplied parts and the result of the previous audit. The standard frequency is as follows.

| Risk class | Typical supplier | Process audit | System audit | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | Safety-relevant parts, level 2 or 3 escalation, rating D | Every 6 months | Every 12 months | 3 to 4 days |
| Medium | Electronic modules, rating C | Every 12 months | Every 24 months | 2 to 3 days |
| Low | Standard parts, rating A or B | Every 24 months | Every 36 months | 1 to 2 days |

A system audit examines the quality management system, including the control of records, the trace test and the handling of non-conforming material. A process audit follows a part through the production steps and checks the controls on the shop floor against the control plan. Audits are normally announced at least 15 working days in advance. Aurelia may also make an unannounced visit, with 24 hours notice, where a serious quality issue has occurred or where records have not been available in the time required.

6.7 Audit conduct and follow-up

Each audit ends with a closing meeting at which the auditor presents findings. Findings are graded as major, minor or observation. A major finding means a requirement is not met or a risk to the customer exists. The supplier must send an action plan within 10 working days of the closing meeting for a major finding and within 20 working days for a minor finding. Evidence that actions have been carried out must be delivered by the date set in the plan, which is normally within 90 days for a major finding. A supplier's audit score is included in the scorecard and affects its risk class for the following year. The supplier must give auditors access to production areas, test equipment, records and, with reasonable notice, to its own sub-tier sources that are named in the traceability chain.

## Annex A Revision history

| Revision | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2021-03-01 | First edition in English. |
| 3 | 2024-01-01 | Clause 7.2 read: "A change of coating or surface treatment within the same specification family requires notification to Aurelia at least 60 days before implementation; approval is not required." |
| 4 | 2026-07-01 | Section 7 rewritten; see clause 7.1. |

## Annex D Service parts supplied through Aurelia Ricambi

For service parts of discontinued models supplied through Aurelia Ricambi (a separate company of the group), a change of coating requires notification only. This annex does not apply to series production parts.

title: Nordhavn supplier requirements, rev 2 (excerpt)
text:
# Nordhavn supplier requirements, rev 2 (excerpt)

## 1. Scope, applicability and order of precedence

1.1 Purpose of this manual

This manual sets out the customer specific requirements of Nordhavn Trucks AB ("Nordhavn") for organisations that supply production material, service parts, tooling or related services for Nordhavn trucks and vans. It supplements the quality management system requirements that each supplier already operates under its own certification. It does not replace them. Where Nordhavn asks for something beyond the baseline, this manual says so explicitly and gives the reason, the expected evidence and the contact responsible.

Nordhavn builds heavy trucks at its Södertälje plant (about 118 vehicles per day on two shifts), medium trucks and chassis cabs at its Gdańsk plant (about 64 per day) and light vans at its Örebro plant (about 210 per day). Because these plants share suppliers, a single set of requirements is used for all three.

1.2 Who the manual applies to

The manual applies to every legal entity that holds, or is being considered for, a purchase relationship with Nordhavn for the items listed in 1.3. It applies to the entity named on the purchase order and to every manufacturing site that produces, finishes, tests or packs the item. The supplier is responsible for making sure its own sub-tier suppliers meet the requirements that affect the product, and for passing those requirements down through its own purchasing terms.

The manual does not apply to suppliers of office supplies, canteen services, travel, or general facilities maintenance, unless they work on a production line or in a production area. Such suppliers follow the site access rules of the plant they visit.

1.3 Categories of supply covered

Suppliers are grouped into categories. The category determines how much of the manual applies and how often Nordhavn reviews the supplier. The group is set by Nordhavn Purchasing when the supplier is first entered in the supplier system, and the supplier is told its category in writing.

| Category | Description | Typical annual spend with Nordhavn (SEK) | Share of manual that applies |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Safety-relevant or function-critical production parts (brake components, steering parts, cab structure, electronic control units) | Above 40 million | Full |
| B | Other series production parts and assemblies | 8 to 40 million | Full, except the extended on-site audit programme |
| C | Standard catalogue parts, fasteners, consumables used in production | 1 to 8 million | Core requirements only |
| D | Service parts and accessories | Any | Core requirements plus packaging and labelling |
| E | Production tooling, gauges and test equipment | Any | Tooling and measurement requirements only |
| F | Logistics, sequencing, sorting and rework services | Any | Service requirements only |

The "core requirements" are those on supplier identification, quality planning, product and process evidence, measurement, nonconforming product handling, traceability and record retention. Each later chapter marks any requirement that applies to a smaller group of categories.

1.4 Relationship to purchase orders

A purchase order is the commercial and technical instruction to deliver. This manual is the standing quality framework that sits behind every purchase order. The two are read together in the following way.

1.4.1 The manual is incorporated by reference into each purchase order, framework agreement and call-off schedule that Nordhavn issues. The supplier does not need to sign it again for each order. Placing a delivery against an order is treated as acknowledgement that the supplier has the current edition of the manual and will follow it.

1.4.2 A purchase order may add requirements specific to one part, one programme or one delivery. Such additions apply only to that order and do not change how the manual reads for any other order.

1.4.3 The purchase order carries the quantity, price, delivery date, delivery address, part number and drawing level. The manual never overrides those commercial fields.

1.4.4 The manual carries the quality planning, evidence and audit requirements. Where a purchase order is silent on a quality topic, the manual applies in full.

1.4.5 A supplier that believes the manual and a purchase order cannot both be met must raise the question with the Nordhavn buyer named on the order before it ships. Delivering first and raising the question afterwards does not alter the order of precedence below.

1.5 Order of precedence

When two documents give different instructions on the same point, the higher item in the following list prevails. A supplier must not choose between them on its own judgement.

| Rank | Document | What it governs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Applicable law and regulation in the country of manufacture and the country of delivery | Legal duties of every party |
| 2 | The product drawing, model data and technical specification named on the purchase order | Product definition and acceptance criteria |
| 3 | Special requirements written on the purchase order for that order only | One-off or programme-specific instructions |
| 4 | This manual | Quality planning, evidence, audit and performance expectations |
| 5 | The framework agreement and general terms of purchase | Commercial and legal terms that are not quality topics |
| 6 | The supplier's own procedures and standard terms | Internal methods of the supplier |

The supplier's own standard terms of sale do not apply to Nordhavn orders, even if they are printed on an order acknowledgement, a delivery note or an invoice. Where the supplier's own procedure is stricter than this manual, the supplier follows its own procedure, because the manual sets a minimum.

1.6 Relationship to the supplier's certification and to other customers

A supplier is expected to hold a current third-party certificate of its quality management system, issued by a certification body that is itself accredited. Nordhavn accepts the certificate as evidence of the baseline system. A certificate is not evidence that the supplier meets the additional requirements in this manual, and Nordhavn audits against those additions separately.

Suppliers that serve other vehicle makers use one set of processes for all customers wherever possible. Nordhavn does not require a dedicated line, a dedicated team or a separate quality system. It does require that Nordhavn-specific requirements are visible in the supplier's own planning documents so that operators and inspectors can see them.

1.7 Language, units and format

The working language of the manual and of all supplier submissions is English. Drawings may remain in the language in which they were issued. Dimensions are in millimetres, mass in kilograms, torque in newton metres and temperature in degrees Celsius, unless the drawing states otherwise. Dates are written in the form year-month-day. Submissions are made through the Nordhavn Supplier Portal; email attachments are used only when the portal is unavailable and only when the buyer has agreed.

1.8 Retention and confidentiality

The supplier keeps quality records relating to Nordhavn products for the life of the vehicle programme plus 15 years, or for the period set by law if longer. Drawings, specifications and data supplied by Nordhavn remain the property of Nordhavn, are used only to fulfil Nordhavn orders and are not passed to a third party without the written consent of the Nordhavn buyer.

1.9 Contacts and interpretation

Questions about how the manual applies are sent first to the Supplier Quality Engineer assigned to the supplier. If that person cannot settle the point within 5 working days, the question moves to the Supplier Quality Manager of the relevant plant, and then to the Head of Supplier Quality at group level. Interpretations given in writing by the Head of Supplier Quality apply to all suppliers in the same category.

## 2. Definitions and abbreviations

2.1 How to use this glossary

The terms below have the meaning given here wherever they appear in this manual and in Nordhavn purchase orders. Where an industry term is used more widely than Nordhavn uses it, only the Nordhavn meaning applies. Terms are grouped by topic so that related ideas can be read together. A supplier that uses different names internally is free to do so, but submissions to Nordhavn must use the terms below.

2.2 Quality planning and product approval terms

| Term | Abbreviation | Meaning in this manual |
|---|---|---|
| Advanced Product Quality Planning | APQP | The structured method a supplier uses to plan a new or modified product from concept to series production. Nordhavn expects five phases and a named cross-functional team of at least 5 people. |
| Production Part Approval Process | PPAP | The set of evidence that shows the supplier's process can make parts that meet every requirement at the quoted rate. The evidence is submitted to Nordhavn for each part number. |
| Part Submission Warrant | PSW | The summary sheet that opens a PPAP submission. It names the part, the drawing level, the reason for submission, the quantity produced and the signatory at the supplier. |
| Control plan | CP | A written description of the checks, controls and reactions used at each step of production, from receiving through to shipping. |
| Process flow diagram | PFD | A step-by-step picture of the manufacturing route, including transport, storage, rework and sorting steps. |
| Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (design) | DFMEA | Analysis by the design owner of how a product could fail to function and what the effect would be. |
| Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (process) | PFMEA | Analysis of how each process step could fail to make a conforming part, ranked by severity, occurrence and detection. |
| Risk priority number | RPN | The product of severity, occurrence and detection scores, each on a scale of 1 to 10. It is a ranking aid only. |
| Action priority | AP | A rating of High, Medium or Low given to a failure cause. Nordhavn uses it in preference to RPN when both are available. |
| Special characteristic | SC | A product or process feature identified by Nordhavn or the supplier as needing extra control because of its effect on safety, regulation or fit and function. |
| Design record | | The drawing, model data or specification that defines the product. |
| Dimensional results | | The measured values for every dimension on the drawing, taken on a sample of at least 6 parts from the production tool or cavity. |
| Run-at-rate | R@R | A production trial at the quoted hourly volume, normally for 8 consecutive hours, to confirm that people, equipment and material flow can meet demand. |
| Sample part | | A part from the same process as series parts, kept as a reference for appearance, colour or feel. |
| Gate review | | A planned point in APQP at which the team and Nordhavn confirm that the work so far is complete enough to continue. |

2.3 Measurement and statistical terms

| Term | Abbreviation | Meaning in this manual |
|---|---|---|
| Measurement System Analysis | MSA | The study of how much of the variation seen in measured data comes from the gauge, the method or the person measuring, rather than from the product. |
| Gauge repeatability and reproducibility | GR&R | An MSA study giving the share of tolerance or total variation used by the measurement system. Nordhavn expects at least 10 parts, 3 appraisers and 3 repeats. |
| Bias | | The difference between the average of repeated measurements and a reference value. |
| Linearity | | The change in bias across the working range of a gauge. |
| Stability | | The change in a measurement over time when the same part is measured. |
| Number of distinct categories | ndc | The number of groups of parts the measurement system can reliably tell apart. Nordhavn expects 5 or more. |
| Statistical Process Control | SPC | The use of control charts and related methods to watch a process and to react before it produces nonconforming parts. |
| Control chart | | A time-ordered chart of a measured value with a centre line and calculated control limits. |
| Capability index | Cp | The tolerance width divided by six standard deviations of the process. It describes spread only. |
| Capability index, centred | Cpk | The smaller of the distances from the mean to each limit, divided by three standard deviations. It describes spread and centring. |
| Preliminary performance index | Ppk | The same calculation as Cpk but using the overall standard deviation, normally for early studies of at least 100 consecutive parts. |
| Rational subgroup | | A small group of parts made under the same conditions, used to separate short-term from long-term variation. |
| Attribute data | | Data that can only be counted or classed, such as pass or fail. |
| Variable data | | Data that is measured on a continuous scale. |

Nordhavn's usual targets are a Ppk of at least 1.67 for the first submission of a special characteristic and a Cpk of at least 1.33 in series production, unless the purchase order states otherwise.

2.4 Supplier performance and delivery terms

| Term | Abbreviation | Meaning in this manual |
|---|---|---|
| Parts per million | ppm | Nonconforming parts found at Nordhavn per million parts delivered, calculated monthly for each part family. |
| Supplier quality rating | SQR | The monthly score from 0 to 100 combining ppm, delivery, responsiveness and audit results. |
| On-time delivery | OTD | The share of delivery lines received within the window of 1 day early to 0 days late. |
| Corrective action report | 8D | The eight-discipline method for containing a problem, finding its cause and preventing recurrence. |
| Containment | | Action taken at once to stop suspect parts from reaching the vehicle line or the customer. |
| Root cause | | The underlying reason a problem occurred and was not detected. |
| Escape | | A nonconforming part that leaves the supplier and is found later. |
| Traceability | | The ability to follow a part, batch or serial number back to material, machine, shift and date. |
| First in, first out | FIFO | Stock handling in which the oldest stock is used or shipped first. |
| Lot | | The quantity made under one set of conditions with one batch of input material. |

2.5 Organisation, audit and commercial terms

| Term | Abbreviation | Meaning in this manual |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier Quality Engineer | SQE | The Nordhavn employee responsible for the quality relationship with a named group of suppliers. |
| Quality management system | QMS | The set of processes a supplier uses to plan, control and improve quality. |
| Process audit | | An on-site check of how a process runs against its control plan and work instructions. |
| Product audit | | A check of finished parts against the full drawing and specification. |
| Sub-tier supplier | | Any organisation that supplies material or service to the supplier rather than to Nordhavn. |
| Series production | | Production for sale in vehicles, after launch has finished. |
| Launch | | The period from the first production-intent parts to stable series output. |
| Tier 1 | | A supplier that sells directly to Nordhavn. |
| Purchase order | PO | The order document that instructs a supplier to deliver. |
| Request for quotation | RFQ | The invitation to a supplier to offer a price and technical solution. |
| Capacity | | The maximum output a supplier can sustain, expressed in parts per week at stated shifts and efficiency. |

2.6 Conventions

The word "must" marks a requirement. "Should" marks a strong expectation that the supplier may depart from only with a documented reason. "May" marks a permission. "Working day" means a day that is not a weekend or public holiday at the Nordhavn plant that placed the order. Where a number of days is given without qualification, calendar days are meant.

## 3. Supplier selection and onboarding

3.1 Principles

Nordhavn chooses suppliers on evidence of capability, capacity, financial stability and willingness to work to the requirements in this manual. Price is considered only among suppliers that have passed the technical and commercial checks described here. A supplier is told at the start which steps apply to its category and how long each is expected to take. The target for the whole route, from the first questionnaire to the supplier's entry in the supplier system, is 14 weeks for category A and B, and 6 weeks for categories C to F.

3.2 Stages of selection

| Stage | Activity | Owner at Nordhavn | Target duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Introduction and confidentiality agreement | Purchasing | 1 week |
| 2 | Self-assessment questionnaire | Supplier Quality | 2 weeks |
| 3 | Capacity check | Purchasing and Logistics | 2 weeks |
| 4 | Financial check | Finance | 2 weeks |
| 5 | Site visit and process review | Supplier Quality | 3 weeks |
| 6 | Selection panel decision | Purchasing, Supplier Quality, Engineering | 1 week |
| 7 | Set-up in the supplier system and portal training | Purchasing | 3 weeks |

Stages 3 and 4 may run at the same time. Stage 5 is normally skipped for categories C and F when the supplier already holds a current certificate of its quality system and a satisfactory result from the capacity check.

3.3 Self-assessment questionnaire

The questionnaire is sent through the portal and has 96 questions in 8 sections: organisation and ownership, quality management, product planning, production control, measurement, logistics and traceability, people and training, and environment and workplace safety. The supplier answers each question with a score of 0 to 4 and attaches evidence for every answer above 2. The supplier's managing director or plant manager signs the questionnaire to confirm that it is complete and accurate.

Nordhavn scores each section on a maximum of 100 points and weights the sections as follows.

| Section | Weight |
|---|---|
| Quality management | 20% |
| Product planning | 15% |
| Production control | 20% |
| Measurement | 15% |
| Logistics and traceability | 10% |
| People and training | 10% |
| Environment and workplace safety | 5% |
| Organisation and ownership | 5% |

A weighted total of 80 or more allows the supplier to continue without conditions. A total from 65 to 79 allows it to continue if the supplier agrees a written improvement plan with milestones inside 90 days. A total below 65, or a score below 50 in quality management or production control, ends the route. The supplier may reapply after 6 months.

3.4 Capacity check

Nordhavn compares the supplier's demonstrated capacity with the forecast demand for the part family, plus a reserve. The supplier provides, for each relevant machine group, the number of machines, shifts per day, planned working days per year, cycle time, and the efficiency it has achieved in the last 12 months. Nordhavn calculates available capacity and compares it with peak demand.

The standard requirement is that available capacity is at least 125 percent of the peak weekly forecast, where the forecast is taken from the highest 4-week average in the programme plan. For category A parts the requirement is 140 percent. The supplier must also show how it would add capacity if the programme plan were to rise by 20 percent, and how many weeks that would take.

| Item | Category A | Categories B and C | Categories D to F |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum capacity against peak weekly forecast | 140% | 125% | 110% |
| Maximum planned machine utilisation | 80% | 85% | 90% |
| Time to add 20% capacity | 12 weeks or less | 16 weeks or less | 20 weeks or less |
| Days of finished stock held for Nordhavn | 5 | 3 | 2 |
| Single-machine dependency | Backup route needed | Backup route needed for the bottleneck | Not assessed |

Where a part depends on a single tool or a single machine, the supplier must show a recovery plan with the number of days needed to resume output from a standby tool or from a second site.

3.5 Financial check

Nordhavn Finance reviews the supplier's last 3 annual accounts, or fewer for a young company, together with the most recent interim figures. Where the supplier is part of a group, accounts for both the entity and the group are required. Finance also obtains an independent credit rating on a scale of 1 (strongest) to 10.

The measures looked at, and the usual thresholds, are shown below.

| Measure | Usual threshold | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Equity ratio | At least 25% | Lower values need a parent guarantee |
| Current ratio | At least 1.1 | Current assets divided by current liabilities |
| Operating margin, 3-year average | At least 3% | Negative result in any one year is discussed |
| Share of revenue from Nordhavn | No more than 30% | Higher values are discussed with Purchasing |
| Independent credit rating | 6 or better | Rating of 7 or worse leads to a closer review |
| Net debt to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation | No more than 3.5 | Based on the last full year |

A supplier that does not meet a threshold is not excluded automatically. Finance writes a short assessment and may propose a safeguard, such as a payment arrangement, a parent guarantee or a second source. Financial information is kept confidential and is seen only by Finance, the head of Purchasing and the panel members.

3.6 Site visits

A site visit is made by a team of two or three people: a Supplier Quality Engineer, a representative of Purchasing and, for category A, an engineer from the Nordhavn product group. The visit normally lasts 2 days. The supplier receives the agenda at least 10 working days in advance, together with the list of documents and people it should have ready.

The team follows the production route for a part similar to the one to be supplied, from incoming goods to dispatch. It reviews the control of the process, calibration and storage of gauges, handling of nonconforming material, labelling, cleanliness, housekeeping and the safety of people working at the line. It also talks with operators, to see whether instructions are understood and used.

Each observation is scored on the same 0 to 4 scale as the questionnaire. The visit report gives a score for each of the 8 sections and highlights any difference between what the supplier stated in the questionnaire and what the team saw. A difference of more than 15 points in any section is discussed with the supplier's management before the panel meets.

3.7 Selection panel and set-up

The panel looks at the questionnaire result, capacity check, financial assessment, site visit findings and the supplier's quotation. It records the reasons for its decision in writing and tells the supplier within 5 working days. The supplier is then entered in the supplier system under its category, receives a unique supplier number, and is given access to the portal. Two named people from the supplier, one for quality and one for logistics, attend a half-day portal training given by Nordhavn.

3.8 Supplier obligations during onboarding

The supplier must give truthful and complete answers, host the visit without restriction on areas relevant to the Nordhavn product, name a quality contact who speaks English, and meet the milestones in any improvement plan it has agreed. Nordhavn will not pay for the supplier's time or travel during selection, unless the buyer has agreed this in writing before the stage begins.

## 4. Advanced product quality planning and launch

This section sets out how suppliers to Nordhavn Trucks AB plan, prove and launch production parts for our truck and van programs. It applies to all suppliers of production parts, assemblies and sub-assemblies delivered to the plants in Södertälje, Gothenburg and Ostrava.

**1.1 Scope and principles**

Every supplier must run a cross-functional launch team for each new part number. The team must include, as a minimum, quality, manufacturing engineering, logistics, purchasing and a named launch manager. The launch manager is the single point of contact for the Nordhavn Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE) and must be reachable during plant working hours throughout the launch period.

The launch plan must be built backwards from the Nordhavn Start of Production date (SOP). Nordhavn publishes the SOP and the build-volume ramp for each program. The supplier plan must show every gateway date, the owner of each deliverable and the time buffer to the next gateway. A buffer of less than 10 working days between the last validation activity and the run-at-rate event is treated as a planning risk and must be discussed with the SQE at the next gateway review.

**1.2 Phases and gateways**

Nordhavn uses six phases separated by five gateways. The supplier must hold an internal review before each gateway and send the gateway package to the SQE at least 7 calendar days before the gateway meeting.

| Phase | Name | Gateway at phase end | Typical timing before SOP | Main deliverables |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Concept and nomination | G1 | SOP minus 36 to 30 months | Feasibility study, preliminary risk list, target cost confirmation |
| 1 | Planning | G2 | SOP minus 30 to 24 months | Launch plan, preliminary process flow, preliminary list of special characteristics |
| 2 | Product and process design | G3 | SOP minus 24 to 14 months | Process FMEA, draft control plan, gauge plan, tooling order evidence |
| 3 | Validation | G4 | SOP minus 14 to 6 months | Initial sample parts, capability studies, run-at-rate, packaging trial |
| 4 | Launch and ramp-up | G5 | SOP minus 6 months to SOP plus 3 months | Safe launch execution, ramp-up volumes, logistics proof |
| 5 | Stabilization | Closure review | SOP plus 3 to SOP plus 9 months | Exit from launch containment, lessons learned |

At each gateway the SQE records one of three outcomes: green (continue), yellow (continue with a time-bound action list) or red (stop and re-plan). A yellow outcome requires an action list with owners and due dates, and the supplier must review that list weekly with the SQE until every item is closed. A red outcome stops further tooling and capacity spending that is charged to the program until a repeat gateway meeting has taken place.

**1.3 Gateway entry criteria**

The following criteria are used by the SQE when reviewing a gateway package. They are minimum criteria and the SQE may add program-specific items in writing before the gateway.

1.3.1 At G3, the process flow must cover every operation from incoming material to shipping, and every special characteristic must be linked to at least one process step and one control method. The process FMEA must have an action plan for every failure mode with a severity of 9 or 10 and for every failure mode with a severity of 7 or 8 combined with an occurrence of 4 or higher.

1.3.2 At G4, at least 90 percent of production tooling must be on site and the remaining tooling must have a confirmed delivery date no later than 4 weeks before the run-at-rate event. Measurement systems used for special characteristics must have completed their studies before parts are measured for capability.

1.3.3 At G5, the supplier must show that the run-at-rate result met the targets in section 1.4, that packaging has been tested through a complete delivery loop to the receiving plant, and that trained operators are available on every shift planned for the ramp.

**1.4 Run-at-rate**

The run-at-rate event proves that the production process can make good parts at the quoted rate using production tooling, production gauges, production operators and material from the planned sub-suppliers. It is not a laboratory exercise and it must not use hand-finished parts or special staffing.

| Parameter | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Minimum duration | 8 continuous hours or 300 parts, whichever takes longer |
| Target rate | 100 percent of the quoted hourly rate for the peak week of the Nordhavn ramp plan |
| Minimum accepted rate | 95 percent of target rate, measured as good parts divided by planned parts |
| First-time-through yield | 97.0 percent or higher at the final inspection |
| Overall equipment effectiveness at bottleneck | 85 percent or higher during the run |
| Scrap and rework | Recorded by cause code; rework above 3.0 percent of parts needs an action plan |
| Cycle time evidence | Time study for each operation, showing the slowest operation at 90 percent or less of takt time |
| Witness | SQE or a delegate may attend in person; the supplier must provide a live data feed if attendance is not possible |

If the supplier makes the same part number on several lines, each line that is planned for Nordhavn volume must complete its own run-at-rate. A line that supplies less than 20 percent of the planned volume may be excused from a full-length run if the SQE agrees to a shorter run of 4 hours, but the targets in the table remain the same.

When the run does not reach the targets, the supplier must analyze the loss by cause, correct the process and repeat the run. The repeat must start from a clean line, with a new shift handover, and must not reuse data from the first run.

**1.5 Launch containment**

Launch containment, called Safe Launch at Nordhavn, is an additional layer of control that applies from the first production delivery. Its aim is to find process weaknesses before they reach the assembly line. Safe Launch is carried out by the supplier at the supplier site and is separate from any inspection at the Nordhavn goods-receiving area.

| Level | Applies to | Controls | Minimum duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Safe Launch 1 | All parts in the first 3 production batches | 100 percent inspection of all special characteristics at a separate inspection point; first-piece and last-piece checks at every shift; daily data summary to the SQE | 3 batches or 4 weeks, whichever is longer |
| Safe Launch 2 | Parts that meet Safe Launch 1 exit criteria | Sampling at twice the normal control plan frequency; weekly data summary to the SQE; certified inspector on each shift | 12,000 parts or 90 calendar days, whichever is longer |
| Normal control | Parts that meet Safe Launch 2 exit criteria | Frequency of the control plan | Ongoing |

1.5.1 The exit from Safe Launch 1 requires 3 consecutive batches with no nonconformance on a special characteristic, a Cpk of 1.67 or higher for every special characteristic that is measured by variable data, and no open actions from the G5 review.

1.5.2 The exit from Safe Launch 2 requires 90 consecutive days with no Nordhavn line stoppage that is caused by the part, fewer than 50 parts per million rejected at the Nordhavn line, and no open customer complaint on the part number.

1.5.3 Safe Launch inspection records must be kept at the supplier and must be shown to the SQE on request. Records must carry the batch number, the inspector, the date and time, the gauge identification and the measured value for each variable characteristic.

1.5.4 Parts that have passed through Safe Launch inspection must be identified on the box label with the letters SL and the level number, so that the Nordhavn goods-receiving area can recognize them.

**1.6 Ramp-up performance measures**

During phases 4 and 5 the supplier must report these measures to the SQE every week: delivery performance against the call-off schedule (target 98 percent on time and in full), parts per million rejected at Nordhavn, number of open actions, premium freight events and the stock on hand expressed in days of Nordhavn demand. The minimum safety stock during ramp-up is 5 working days of peak demand unless the SQE and the Nordhavn logistics planner agree a different figure in writing.

## 5. Measurement systems and statistical process control

This section defines the requirements for measurement systems, capability studies and ongoing process monitoring. It applies to every characteristic that is listed on a supplier control plan for a Nordhavn part, with the strictest rules reserved for special characteristics.

**2.1 General requirements for measurement systems**

2.1.1 Every gauge, instrument and test fixture used to accept product must have a unique identification number, a calibration record and a named owner. The calibration interval must be set by risk and use. The default interval is 12 months for hand tools such as calipers and micrometers, 6 months for fixtures that are used on more than one shift, and 12 months for coordinate measuring machines with a verification check each week using a reference artefact.

2.1.2 Calibration must be traceable to a national standard through a laboratory with a documented scope of accreditation that covers the quantity, range and uncertainty used. The expanded calibration uncertainty must not exceed 10 percent of the tolerance of the characteristic that is measured.

2.1.3 The resolution of a gauge must be 10 percent or less of the tolerance. For a feature with a total tolerance of 0.20 mm the smallest displayed step must therefore be 0.02 mm or finer. A resolution of 5 percent or less is preferred for special characteristics.

2.1.4 Gauges that are found out of calibration at the time of recalibration require a documented look-back to the last good calibration. The look-back must list the part numbers and batches that were measured with the gauge in that period and must state the result of the impact assessment.

**2.2 Variable gauge studies**

A gauge repeatability and reproducibility study (gauge R&R) is required for every gauge that measures a special characteristic and for every gauge that is new to the control plan. The study must be done with production parts that cover the full process spread, not with parts that are chosen only from the middle of the tolerance.

| Study element | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Study design | 10 parts, 3 appraisers, 3 trials (90 readings); 5 parts, 2 appraisers, 3 trials if only one appraiser is qualified |
| Method | Average and range or analysis of variance; analysis of variance is required where an interaction between part and appraiser is suspected |
| Denominator for percent | Tolerance for characteristics with a two-sided tolerance, total process variation for characteristics that are monitored by chart |
| Acceptable result | Gauge R&R of 10 percent or less |
| Conditional result | Above 10 percent and up to 30 percent, only for non-special characteristics and only with a written justification covering cost and risk |
| Not acceptable | Above 30 percent |
| Number of distinct categories | 5 or higher |
| Special characteristics | Gauge R&R of 10 percent or less on tolerance; no conditional result is permitted |

The study must be repeated when the gauge is repaired, when the method is changed, and at least every 24 months for gauges on special characteristics. It must be repeated sooner when the process capability result is influenced by measurement variation, which is the case when the observed Cpk is more than 0.20 lower than the Cpk that is expected from process data taken with a better instrument.

2.2.1 Bias, linearity and stability must be assessed for gauges that measure special characteristics. Bias must not exceed 5 percent of the tolerance at any reference point. Stability is shown with a control chart of a master part measured every shift for at least 25 shifts.

**2.3 Attribute gauges and visual inspection**

2.3.1 Go and no-go gauges must be verified against a master at the interval in the calibration plan, with a default of 3 months for gauges in daily use.

2.3.2 Attribute and visual inspection must be assessed with an agreement study using at least 50 samples, 3 appraisers and 2 trials. The samples must include at least 30 percent defective parts near the limit. The kappa value between each appraiser and the reference decision must be 0.90 or higher, and the effectiveness against the reference must be 90 percent or higher.

2.3.3 Boundary samples, in the form of physical or photographic limit samples, must be on every inspection station where appearance is judged. Limit samples must be replaced at least every 12 months or when they show wear.

**2.4 Capability targets**

Capability is shown with Ppk for the initial study and Cpk for ongoing monitoring. The targets are given by the classification of the characteristic.

| Characteristic class | Initial study Ppk | Ongoing Cpk | Initial study size |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC-A, safety and regulatory | 1.67 or higher | 1.67 or higher | 125 consecutive parts, or 25 subgroups of 5 |
| SC-B, function critical | 1.67 or higher | 1.33 or higher | 100 consecutive parts, or 20 subgroups of 5 |
| SC-C, fit and assembly | 1.33 or higher | 1.33 or higher | 100 consecutive parts, or 20 subgroups of 5 |
| Non-special | Not required unless in the control plan | 1.00 or higher where charted | As defined in the control plan |

2.4.1 Initial studies must be run on parts from the production process with production tooling and with one cavity or one fixture per study. For multi-cavity tools each cavity must be studied separately, and the weakest cavity result is the result that is reported.

2.4.2 Data must be tested for normality. Where the data are not normally distributed, the supplier must use a method that is suitable for the distribution, such as a transformation or a percentile method, and must state the method in the study report. The use of a Cpk formula that is built for normal data on skewed data is not permitted.

2.4.3 A process whose Cpk is between 1.00 and the target must have 100 percent inspection of the characteristic until the Cpk meets the target. A process whose Cpk is below 1.00 must have 100 percent inspection and a corrective action plan with a date for the return to target.

2.4.4 For characteristics that are measured only by attribute data, capability is shown by a run of 300 consecutive parts with no nonconformance for SC-C and 500 consecutive parts for SC-A and SC-B.

**2.5 Sampling and control charting**

2.5.1 Control charts are required for every SC-A and SC-B characteristic that is measured by variable data. For SC-C and non-special characteristics, charts are required where the Cpk is below 1.67 or where the control plan states it.

2.5.2 The default chart is an average and range chart with a subgroup of 5 consecutive parts. For slow processes with fewer than 50 parts per shift, an individuals and moving range chart may be used, with a reading each hour.

| Characteristic class | Default sampling frequency | Subgroup or sample size | Chart type |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC-A | Every 30 minutes, and at start of each shift and after each tool change | 5 | Average and range |
| SC-B | Every hour | 5 | Average and range |
| SC-C | Every 2 hours | 3 to 5 | Average and range or individuals |
| Non-special | As defined in the control plan | As defined in the control plan | Not required |

2.5.3 Control limits must be calculated from at least 25 subgroups of stable data and must be recalculated only after a documented process improvement. Specification limits must never be drawn on an average chart as if they were control limits.

2.5.4 The following signals require action: one point beyond a control limit, 7 consecutive points on one side of the center line, 7 consecutive points rising or falling, and 2 of 3 points in the zone beyond two standard deviations on the same side. The reaction for each signal must follow the plan in the next section on special characteristics.

2.5.5 For processes with short runs, such as fewer than 300 parts per batch, the supplier may use a target chart that plots deviation from nominal. The method must be documented and used consistently.

**2.6 Data retention and access**

The supplier must keep gauge studies, capability studies and control charts for the life of the part plus 15 years. Data must be available to the SQE within 2 working days of a request, in a format that allows the raw values to be reviewed and not only the summary figures.
